$comment: P69 (lane lm, D-OPT-DCE-DELETES-A-RELOCATABLE-MEMBERS-HIDDEN-DEFINITIONS): a static-library member's hidden definitions belong to the IMAGE that links the member — the link that pulls it resolves them by name. Each arm's `dependsOn` builds lib.c (a hidden function, a hidden datum and one plain control, nothing in lib.c using the hidden pair) into the pair's static library; main.c links it and uses all three. Exit 42 iff they arrived (lib_version() == 1, 40 + 1 + 1). ✔MEASURED before the fix with the lane's dsscp: a release member (`elf64-x86_64-linux-staticlib`) defined the plain control ALONE — DCE rooted only `isExternallyVisible` definitions, an image question, while a member's definitions are named by the OTHER inputs of its link — where gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 at `-O2 -c` keep both hidden definitions (probe-reference-cc run 20261001-152924-ba09ffc4). The fix: a static-archive member is optimized as a `opt::ModuleExtent::LinkInput`, which roots every external-linkage definition. The release arm builds the library under the release pipeline too, so it is the witness (the defect was release-only). lib_version's loop is there for the optimizer to fold: ✔MEASURED 2026-10-01 with the lane's dsscp, the release library and the release executable both differ from the baseline ones on all five pairs (without the loop the library did not — nothing in it was left to optimize once the hidden pair is kept), so both levels carry `mustDifferFromBaseline` and the arm proves the member WAS optimized and still kept the hidden pair.
